title: Cut the framework's token spend and review time without losing the defects it catches
intent: Every token the framework injects or spends must pay for a defect caught or a gate enforced. The framework measures its own token and time cost from transcripts and the forge, and each change proves its effect against a recorded baseline. The merge gates keep their fail-closed defaults and exit codes. Reviewers keep their verdicts: a prompt change ships only with zero verdict flips on the eval corpus, and reviewers stay on Opus. Review depth follows a tier computed by script from the changed paths, never a self-declared tier. This plan depends on outcome o4 of plan-apexyard-harness-golden-path for the Rex and Hakim trim and adds everything else. Baseline, 2026-10-10 session: main context mean 490k tokens per turn with 18 compactions; the /approve-merge body injected 209 times at 34 KB; every Rex spawn starts at 49k tokens before it reads the diff; 469 CI-wait turns inside 195 reviewer runs; 31 Rex rounds followed a base-branch refresh with an unchanged patch.

outcomes.title: One framework script measures token and time cost per session, per review and per PR, and a dated baseline exists.
The main context stays small: compaction is tuned and prompted, workers start fresh instead of forking, and harness requests are filed with measurements.
A base-branch refresh or a same-SHA reopen with an unchanged patch costs no Rex round.
Reviewers never wait for CI. The orchestrator waits without model turns and spawns Rex after CI is green.
Review and audit agents start without CLAUDE.md and the memory index, the Hakim and Tariq prompts are lean, and a delta re-review uses less reasoning.
Skill bodies on the execution path are short, shared blocks appear once, and ceremony text in skills matches where it finds faults.
Review depth follows a tier computed by script and the review round, with the rail in the spawn path and the merge gate untouched.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A framework script reads a session transcript and reports context tokens per turn, context share by category, skill injections and compactions. Shown by: the script path and its output on the 2026-10-10 transcript.

The same script reads subagent transcripts and reports, per reviewer, the first-turn context, total tokens, tool calls, CI-wait turns, cache rebuilds and cache TTL. It reads the forge for Rex rounds per PR and hours from open to merge. Shown by: a dated baseline file under docs/perf/ with the 2026-10-10 numbers.
Every later outcome names the metric it moves, and its reconciliation evidence cites the script output before and after the change. Shown by: the reconciliation records of this plan.

A spike reports, with numbers, whether the auto-compaction threshold setting bounds the context on 1M-context Opus, and the framework docs state the recommended setting. Shown by: the spike memo under docs/.
The mean context per turn in the next measured session is at most 300k tokens, from 490k. The recommended setting and the compact prompt are in place. Shown by: the o1 script.

parallel-work.md and /fan-out default to a fresh role-appropriate spawn with a written brief. A fork is used only when the needed facts are not yet in a file. Shown by: the rule text and the skill text.

Four harness requests are filed with the measured numbers. They cover skill-body dedupe inside one window, and a fork from a compacted parent or with a context budget. They also cover re-injection as names only, and no skill listing for agents without the Skill tool. Shown by: the issue links in the plan notes.

After a base-branch refresh, pr-workflow.md step 3 runs rex_approval_carries_over first and asks for a Rex delta only when it returns false. Shown by: the rule text and a test in which a merge commit with a smuggled hunk still blocks.

Carry-over covers chained refreshes when git range-diff is empty and the merge tree equals an isolated merge-tree result. It fails closed otherwise. Shown by: an AgDR-0178 amendment and new cases in test_lib_merge_behind.sh.

A reopen under a new PR number with the same head SHA, base and ticket carries the Rex marker forward with carried_from=<sha>. A CHANGES REQUESTED verdict never carries, and an advisory fix always gets a delta. Shown by: hook tests and the marker field.
Over the next 40 merged framework PRs, pure-refresh Rex rounds are 0 out of the refresh events counted, from 31 in the baseline. Shown by: the o1 script.

The auto-code-review hook prints at most 300 bytes and keeps exit 2 and the pending-review marker. It tells the orchestrator to wait for green CI with a Monitor, then spawn Rex. The /code-review skill says the same. Shown by: the hook text, the skill text and a test.

code-reviewer.md and security-reviewer.md tell a reviewer to run gh pr checks once and never wait. A hook blocks gh pr checks --watch, gh run watch and sleep of 60 seconds or more for review-class agents. Shown by: the agent text, the hook and its test.
A PR with queued checks and a valid Rex marker still blocks at merge. Shown by: a test beside block-merge-on-red-ci.sh.

CI-wait turns per reviewer run are 0 beyond the one check, from 469 turns across 195 runs. Main-loop cache rebuilds during a wait and hours from open to merge are reported beside it. Shown by: the o1 script on the next 40 PRs.

The o4 rule and the getting-started docs tell adopters outside a subscription's limits to set promptCacheTtl to 1h where their provider supports it. Without it, an idle CI wait over 5 minutes rebuilds the main context. Shown by: the docs text and the rule text.

Seven review and audit agents set omitClaudeMd and carry the 8-line floor block: code-reviewer, security-reviewer, solution-architect, contrarian, qa-engineer, dependency-auditor and penetration-tester. A static test fails when one is missing. Build agents keep CLAUDE.md. Shown by: the test and the o1 first-turn context per agent type.

security-reviewer.md and solution-architect.md are each at most 12,000 bytes, with their rationale under docs/agents/ and their ops-root and marker text as one line. A Tariq corpus exists before the cut. Shown by: wc -c, the text-pin tests and zero verdict flips.

A spike confirms the per-agent reasoning effort field. A delta re-review with a prior Rex marker then runs through a lean-effort agent file with the same prompt, on Opus. Zero flips on at least five delta corpus entries. Shown by: the spike memo, an AgDR and an /eval-agents report.

approve-merge SKILL.md is at most 14,000 bytes. Steps 3a, 4 and 6 live in scripts/approve-merge.sh, which prints one line of JSON. Step 5 and the bare tracker_pr_merge line stay inline. Shown by: wc -c, and a test that the script contains no merge command and no approved_by.
The five most-invoked skills in the baseline are each at most 16,000 bytes, with their rationale moved under docs/skills/. Shown by: a 16 KB cap in the wave-1 test.

The Writing rule preamble and the ops-root resolution block appear in each skill as one line that names the shared file. Today the preamble repeats in 45 skills and the inline walk-up in 24. Shown by: a grep test that finds 0 repeats.
The /approve-merge report ends with a one-line /compact suggestion after a successful merge. Shown by: the skill text.
The orbit skill runs Naqid by default on Plan and Slice drafts, and on a Reconciliation only when a status changes or the operator asks. Shown by: the skill text.

A script in the spawn path computes the ceremony tier from the PR file list with a positive allowlist for Lean. Full covers .claude/, CLAUDE.md, handbooks/, roles/, workflows/, templates/, .github/ and docs/agdr/. Full also covers any JSON a hook reads and any docs path a prompt file names. Shown by: the script, its tests and an AgDR-0116 evolution entry.

On the Lean tier, Rex runs a fixed short procedure that keeps the linked issue read with its comments. Rex posts ESCALATE with no marker when the allowlist does not hold. Shown by: the agent text and three docs-only corpus entries with zero flips.
A PR that looks docs-only but changes a hook or a prompt file is reviewed in Full, and block-unreviewed-merge.sh is unchanged. Shown by: a paired adversarial test and the gate's diff.
A reviewer's hand-back to the orchestrator is at most 300 tokens, and a delta round posts a short format instead of the 13-section body. Shown by: the agent text and a test on a posted delta review.
Tokens per Rex review on a Lean PR fall by at least 35% against the o1 baseline mean of 83.7k. Shown by: the o1 script.

The three review skills resume a reviewer only when its hand-back is under 5 minutes old or its context is under 80k tokens. Otherwise they spawn a fresh reviewer with a brief that lists each earlier blocking finding and the commit range, and it re-checks each finding. Shown by: the skill text, zero flips on the delta corpus entries, and at most 1 resume rebuild per 100 reviewer runs, from 4.0.
